**Short version:** The three passages are rewritten below. The definitions in the first list after the passages are my reading of each term, and each needs your check. The passages do not say what `tp2` and `bit-6 boot` mean, and I left a marked placeholder for each.

## Passage 1

```
- Block save. The K rows (the key vectors, one row per token) are stored in blocks of 16 tokens.
  - A run is up to 16 consecutive tokens inside one block.
  - The code transposes the K rows of a run inside CPU registers (rows become columns).
  - The code then writes the result as whole 64-byte lines, with one store instruction per line.
  - When the run does not fill the block, the store is masked (it writes only the bytes that belong to the run).
  - A run of one token still uses the scatter (a store instruction that writes each value to its own address). Every decode step produces a run of one token.
- Sharing. The main thread and the idle main helper threads share the blocks.
  - Each thread takes its next block from one shared counter.
  - The generated plugin chooses the number of helper threads for each pass (one run of the model over a group of tokens). The number is not fixed.
  - The traced runs used 7 helper threads at tp2 (<<DEFINE: tp2>>).
  - Two kinds of call store on the calling thread only:
    - a caller with a single worker (the handwritten plugins and the unit tests)
    - a pass of at most 16 tokens
```

## Passage 2

```
Where write keeps less than read.

"Keeps" means the share of its single-stream speed that a stream still has when other streams run at the same time.

Write keeps less than read in these rows:
- two writers in one DSU (DynamIQ Shared Unit, a group of Arm cores that share one level-3 cache) at the 160 KiB size
- eight writers at any size

In these rows the writers share one path. The path is one of:
- the mesh port of one DSU (the link from the DSU to the rest of the chip)
- the DRAM write ceiling (the highest rate at which main memory accepts writes) [section 8]

Each write stream runs at 32 GB/s. Each read stream runs at 9 to 12 GB/s. So the write streams reach the limit of the shared path with fewer streams than the read streams do.
```

## Passage 3

```
Codex (the AI agent that reviewed the plan) gave a closing assessment. The plan now states it.

The rows (the test configurations in the plan) can show three things:
- whether the gain needs the prefetchers (the hardware units that fetch data before the program asks for it)
- whether the prefetchers target the L3 (the level-3 cache), and whether demand reads (reads that the program itself issues) find their cache lines there
- whether more requests wait at the home nodes (the mesh nodes that serve requests which leave a core group)

The rows alone cannot tell two explanations apart:
- Your explanation: the data is already in the L3 before the core asks for it.
- The alternative: the DSU (DynamIQ Shared Unit, the group of Arm cores that shares this L3) handles the same prefetch requests faster.

The external-fetch count (the number of fetches that leave the DSU) with the L3 on stays "Insufficient data". Two facts about a counter must first be established on the target machine:
- where the counter gets its count (its source)
- which requests the counter includes (its population)

The bit-6 boot (<<DEFINE: bit-6 boot>>) is the only proposed change that acts on your explanation directly.
```

## Definitions that are my reading (check each)

No project term list was available to me in this session. These definitions come from the passages alone.

- **K rows:** the key vectors of the attention cache, one row per token.
- **pass:** one run of the model over a group of tokens.
- **keeps:** the share of single-stream speed that a stream still has when other streams run.
- **DSU:** Arm DynamIQ Shared Unit, a group of cores with one shared level-3 cache.
- **mesh port** and **home nodes:** the link from the DSU to the chip, and the mesh nodes that serve requests from the DSU.
- **Codex:** the AI agent that reviewed the plan.
- **the rows:** the test configurations in the plan.
- **external-fetch count:** the number of fetches that leave the DSU.
- **"ahead of the core":** I read this as "before the core asks for the data".
- **"(section 8)":** I attached it to the DRAM write ceiling only, not to the mesh port.

## Terms without a definition

- **tp2** and **bit-6 boot:** placeholders are in the text. For bit-6 boot, the definition should name the register and say whether the bit is set or cleared.
- **generated plugin**, **handwritten plugins**, **main helper threads:** I kept these names unchanged. Add a clause for each if the surrounding document does not define them earlier.
